_note: The Character Intelligence Lab's reproducible configurations (ADR-275, ADR-290, ADR-333, ADR-336). Cases 1-12, 14 and 15 can be run today; 13 is waiting on P9. Case 9 ran out of blockers when P11 landed the fifth stock considerer, the one that prices a route rather than a place. **Three fixtures**: the original flat world for the explorers, whose every byte matters because case 15's golden trace is taken from it; `guard-post.scene.json` for the decided characters; and `river-crossing.scene.json` for case 9. The third exists because of a constraint that was measured rather than assumed -- a hero stone dropped 90 m away across the river moves 0 of the golden's 3,600 samples, and the same stone 6 m from `scout` moves 1,779 of them by up to 13.685 m. The lab fixture is frozen against a body the explorers can reach, which is the only kind of body a river case could have added.

cases.title: A socket on a hand is on the hand
cases.question: Does a prop attached to a character's hand socket go where the hand is, and can the engine tell that answer from its own fallback?
cases.expectation: `scout` carries four sockets. `hand` names the joint `hand.r` and resolves 2.878 m from the body's own frame; `head` names `head.x` and resolves 4.218 m from it and 1.8 m from the hand. `chest` names no joint and resolves against the entity frame with the skeleton installed, and `tail` names a joint no rig here carries and does the same -- both reported as `SocketResolution::EntityFrame` rather than as success. The lantern node is attached to `hand` and is drawn there. Before ADR-274 every one of the four gave the same answer and all four returned true.
cases.notes: Asserted by tests/unit/test_character_lab_sockets.cpp. Watch the lantern: if it sits inside the alien's chest, `Entity::setSkeleton` is not being called and the socket has silently fallen back.

cases.title: Three wanderers, three seeds, three routes
cases.question: Do characters with different seeds in the same world take different routes, and does the same world twice produce the same routes?
cases.expectation: Over 60 s each of `scout`, `rover` and `diver` walks more than 10 m and stands in at least three distinct 4 m navigation cells (measured: 62.9 m / 11 cells, 72.4 m / 22 cells, 50.8 m / 14 cells), and the three routes separate by up to 28.0 m. Two runs of the identical world agree to 0.000000000 m -- the control, without which 'three routes' would be three samples of noise rather than three characters.
cases.notes: The separation here is the seed's, not taste's: ADR-270 records that every character scores the same global list of interest points -- 140 of them in this fixture, visible to all four bodies -- which is why two Glowmere characters walk the same route.

cases.title: A route round what is in the way
cases.question: Does the planner route around a solid, and does it leave a clear line alone?
cases.expectation: The grid is 54x54 at 4 m: 2,916 cells, 2,517 walkable, 380 water, **19 blocked** by the thirteen solids the heroes contribute, falling into **3 regions** whose largest holds 2,300. `NavGridStats::regions` is computed at build and read by no UI (ADR-268); this is the first thing in the repository that asserts on it. A cross-world request returns a route at least as long as the straight line; a 12 m hop over open ground returns exactly its 12.00 m line; a goal outside the map is refused with a `PathStatus` other than `Ok` rather than with a route somewhere else.
cases.notes: The trap this case cost a wrong conclusion to find: a hero's `position.y` is the obstacle's BASE (`entity::obstaclesFromHeroes`). The first version of this fixture authored heroes at y = 0 over the shipped procedural world, whose ground there is -7.46 m. Thirteen blocking solids were indexed, the log said so, and every one floated 7.46 m above the walker's head -- `penned` strolled out of a sealed pen and 137.86 m across the map, and the measurement read as 'obstacles do not contain a character', which is false. The fixture is a flat world now for exactly that reason.

cases.title: A penned character is stuck and nothing says so
cases.question: What does being stuck look like in the numbers, and is there anything in the engine that reports it?
cases.expectation: `penned` stands inside ten hero stones on a 6 m ring, whose solids overlap by 0.26 m so the wall has no gap a 0.7 m body could take. Over 120 s it walks **0.00 m** and stands in **1 cell**, while `rover` -- the same behaviour, the same clips, no pen -- walks 72.4 m across 22 cells. `Navigator::requestPath` from the middle of the pen to the open world returns **`PathStatus::Unreachable` with 0 waypoints**, and the control -- the same request from just outside the pen -- returns `Ok` with 2. So the engine knows, exactly, and **says nothing**: the status is surfaced to no UI (ADR-268), `Explore`'s `stuckSeconds` watchdog replans silently, and a body whose every goal is behind a wall is indistinguishable, on screen and in the logs, from one that has decided to stand still.
cases.notes: It does not even walk: every destination `Explore` could pick is outside the wall, `pickDestination` rejects them all, and the body idles for two minutes. That is the sharpest form of the defect -- being stuck and being idle produce the same frame.

cases.title: Two minutes, and the scrub against the play
cases.question: Does the world still hold after a long run, and does seeking to a second land where playing to it did?
cases.expectation: After 120 s every body is finite and inside the map. Play-vs-seek measures **0.025000 m at 30 s** -- inside the 90 s replay window, where a scrub is supposed to equal a play -- and 27.834103 m at 120 s, where it is not: a seek past the window starts from `t - 90 s` and costs a body its accumulated history, which is what the window is for. The 30 s figure was **1.360136 m** when this case was written, and ADR-273 is what moved it: `EntityWorld::seek` used to re-simulate a strict subset of `update` -- behaviours only, no interest points, no crowd field, no gait, no action queue, no `applyOffsets` -- and left `BehaviorContext::self` at 0, all of which `Explore` reads. Those were ADR-267's four seek defects and they are now fixed, so the residual is 54x smaller. It is not zero because this is the live tier, which ADR-091 explicitly does not hold to scrub == play; the baked tier is the one that must agree. What is also asserted, and what nothing had checked before this lab, is that seeking twice to the same second lands in the same place. The control is the same simulation at 30 Hz, which must disagree: 1.247820 m.
cases.notes: P1 owns the fixed step and the four seek defects. This case is where the before-number lives, deliberately not in the unit that will move it.

cases.title: Every character used to see everything, and nothing scored an option
cases.question: What does one character know that another does not?
cases.expectation: Nothing, until P2. `EntityWorld::interestPoints()` is one global list -- 141 entries in this fixture (28 landmark, 5 character, 108 water; there is no glow, because this is a flat world with no ecology) -- with no range, no facing, no occlusion and no notion of having noticed something, and every one of the four characters scored all of it every time it picked a goal. **That is still true of `Explore` and it is now a choice rather than the only option**: since ADR-333 its goal model is `entity::goalWeight` behind an `InterestConsiderer` whose `source` is a knob, and it is set to `Omniscient` because five Glowmere characters are explorers and changing which list they score is a changed film. At 2 s, `scout` (range 60 m) holds 20 percepts reaching 39.23 m and `rover` (range 12 m) holds 2 reaching 11.59 m. What has changed since this case was written is the last sentence: the four navigating behaviours still report a destination through `NavDebug` and now something **does** report the score it beat -- `IBehavior::decisionDebug`, which `explore` deliberately does not implement and `decide` does. Case 14 is where the scores are printed.
cases.notes: The before-arm, kept. The 141-entry omniscient list is still what `Explore` reads; the percepts beside it are what a `decide` character reads instead, and case 14 is the after-arm. **This fixture is frozen**: case 15's golden position trace is taken from it, and adding one body changes what the other five perceive and score.

cases.title: Investigating a mushroom
cases.question: Does a character notice a glowing thing it was not already going to, approach it, and attend to it while it is there?
cases.expectation: It does. `investigate` (ADR-333) is the first thing in this engine to read a percept: it scores `DecisionContext::percepts` -- never `interestPoints()` -- at `salience x the decider's own taste x staleness`, emits one option carrying a `Move` to a stand-off point, a `Face` at the thing and a `Pose` of the `observe` activity, and the selector pushes that onto `Authority::Routine`. Measured on a hand-written pair of percepts: a `Glow` percept at 2 m with salience 0.95 beside a `Character` percept at 12 m with salience 0.60, through a considerer told `kinds: ["character"]`, picks the **character** -- the brighter, nearer, more salient mushroom loses to the filter. The control is the identical percepts through `kinds: ["glow"]`, which picks the mushroom. The staleness arm: the same percept four seconds older scores **nothing** at `staleSeconds: 4`, and two seconds older scores between that and the fresh value. `approach` is a stand-off and it is load-bearing -- see case 14.
cases.notes: The brief's second scenario. Asserted by tests/unit/test_entity_decision.cpp. **The glow percept is scripted, and the reason is a fixture gap rather than an engine one**: a `Glow` interest point comes from a terrain node's `world::GlowCluster` list (composition.cpp:glowInterestPoints) and neither character fixture grows one -- the lab's 141 points are 28 landmark / 5 character / 108 water and guard-post's 8 are 5 landmark / 3 character, because both are flat worlds with no ecology. `ScriptedPerception` is what ADR-290 built for exactly this, and the live arm on the identical code path is case 14's guard, which investigates a `Character` percept the grid produced. A fixture with ecology would close the gap and is the smallest thing this case still wants.

cases.title: A social interaction
cases.question: Do two characters notice each other, and does one change what it was doing because of the other?
cases.expectation: One does. On `guard-post.scene.json`, `sentry` holds a post at (-34, -6) and `courier` patrols the line x = -16 under a list of authored `move` actions; their closest approach is 18 m and the sentry's sense range is 24, so the courier is an `InterestKind::Character` percept for part of each leg and not for the rest. **And the losing scores are beside the winner**, which is the overlay this lab owed: at the moment it commits, `IBehavior::decisionDebug` reports `post = 3.80, investigate = 4.04, idle = 0.10`; ten seconds later, with the courier gone, `post = 1.00, investigate = 0.07, idle = 0.10` and the post has it back. Over 75 s the sentry goes **13.442 m** from its post, is more than 2 m from it on 2,791 frames, takes 9 decisions and refuses one switch on the margin. The control is the same body with `entity/sentry/decide/investigate/weight` driven to 0: **0.000 m**, which is also the ADR-225 arm -- a weight the engine read once from the JSON would not be reachable by that knob.
cases.notes: The brief's fourth scenario. Asserted by tests/unit/test_entity_decision.cpp. `ActionQueue` already had the authority tiers, preemption and resumption this needs and it still does all of the doing: the decider's whole output is an `ActionDesc` list pushed onto `Authority::Routine` with `override`, so a director shot still preempts a decision exactly as it preempts a schedule.

cases.title: Crossing a river
cases.question: Does a character choose between fording a river and walking round it, and can it say why?
cases.expectation: It does, and the reason is arithmetic rather than a rule. `route` (ADR-336) is the fifth stock considerer and the only thing in this engine that prices a *way* instead of a place: it asks `Navigator::requestPath` twice with the same request and two different `NavPathCost::wadePenalty` -- 0, which fords, and 40, which goes round -- and scores both with the character's own price on a wet metre, `length + wadePenalty x the metres of the route in water`. On this fixture, from (-70, -8) to the far bank at (-66, 46), the two ways are **54.15 m with 11.26 weighted wet metres** and **84.56 m with 1.61**. At `wadePenalty` 0.4 the ford scores **0.4055** against the detour's **0.3195** and wins; at 12.0 it scores **0.1745** against **0.2781** and loses. Same world, same two routes, one knob. On screen over 150 s with one body at each taste: the wader crosses water **1.40 m** deep and never goes east of x = -66; the drylander's deepest is **0.27 m**, clipping the shallow tip where the channel ends, and it goes east to x = -39. Both reach the bank, and at 2 s the overlay reads `north-bank = 0.4125, north-bank round = 0.3185, idle = 0.0500` for the wader and `0.1760 / 0.3262 / 0.0500` for the drylander. Two controls that are not tastes. `guard-post.scene.json` is the same flat world with no river, and the same considerer over it publishes **one** way and not two. And `plodder`, a third body in this fixture with one authored `move` straight at the far bank and no decider at all, wades **1.40 m** -- which is what an option whose single action named the destination would have done, and is why the winner's actions are a `Move` per waypoint of the route that was priced.
cases.notes: The brief's third scenario, and the gate on the Glowmere Valley 3 showcase -- whose second demonstration is a jetpack alien crossing the river while a walking-only one routes around it, which is exactly the two bodies in this fixture. Asserted by tests/unit/test_route_pricing.cpp. Two things this case cost a wrong answer to find. **An option has to be the route and not the destination**: `NavigatorPath::route` answers a `move` with the straight line and leaves the rest to local steering, which cannot get a body round a lake, so the first version reported the detour in the overlay while the body waded. The winner's actions are now a `Move` per waypoint of the route that was priced. And **the driest way is not a dry way**: the detour clips 1.61 weighted wet metres at the river's tip because that is cheaper than sixty more dry metres, which is the planner being right; the assertion is the seven-to-one ratio rather than a zero the fixture would have had to be bent to produce.

cases.title: Two characters, two ranges, two different worlds
cases.question: Does what a character notices depend on the numbers its author wrote, and is the range the thing that made the difference?
cases.expectation: At 2 s on the shared 140-entry interest list, `scout` (range 60 m, 200 deg) holds **20 percepts reaching 39.23 m** and `rover` (range 12 m, same capacity, same cadence) holds **2 reaching 11.59 m**. Neither working set is full, so "fewer" means noticed fewer and not allowed to hold fewer. The control that isolates the range is the *same body twice*: `scout` at 60 m holds 20 percepts and `scout` with its `entity/scout/perception/range` parameter driven to 12 holds **4, a strict subset**, from the same position to within a micrometre -- so the difference is the number and not the place the body was standing. Facing is the second arm: `diver` at 90 deg holds **10** percepts and the same body at 360 holds **24**, again a strict superset. A percept is stale by design: the stalest Character percept at 4 Hz is **0.150 s old and 0.225 m behind the body it names**, which is one cadence period of a 1.5 m/s walk.
cases.notes: Asserted by tests/unit/test_entity_perception.cpp. The first version of the staleness arm asserted the opposite -- that a Character percept sits exactly on its body -- and failed by 0.225 m. The assertion was wrong and the engine was right: being wrong about where something is is most of what perception buys over the omniscient list it replaces (ADR-270 section 4).

cases.title: The occlusion budget, and the arm at zero
cases.question: How many sightlines does a crowd spend, and does a percept that was never tested say so?
cases.expectation: Twenty-four bodies either side of an eleven-stone wall, six seconds, one occlusion test per body per second. **Exactly 144 tests are performed** -- `floor(T x testsPerSecond)` per body, not "about that on average", because the schedule is a pure function of the sense tick index rather than an accumulator. 600 sense ticks produce 4,800 percepts from 24,471 candidates; the 4,656 percepts the budget could not reach are left with `tested == false` and **are not dropped** (ADR-270), because a percept discarded when a budget runs out is a character whose behaviour depends on how many other characters exist. 405 frame-observations come back with a tested percept genuinely occluded, which is the arm that says `heroSightline` is measuring something rather than returning 1 the way it does when its `ClearanceField::map` is null. The control is the same crowd with `occlusionTestsPerSecond` driven to 0: **0 tests, `tested == false` on every percept of every body on every one of 360 frames**, and percepts still produced.
cases.notes: The wall is not decoration. `world::heroSightline` knows the ground and the heroes exactly and nothing else, so a crowd over flat ground with no heroes between the bodies would measure a function that can only ever answer 1 -- which is the shape of probe this repository has been caught by twice this week. And the cost of a sightline is a property of the world function, not of the nine rays: 0.008 ms on this flat fixture against 1800.6 us at 20 m on glowmere-valley-2, measured. The budget is justified by the shipped world and a fixture cannot prove it.

cases.title: A head that turns while the legs keep walking
cases.question: Can this engine put anything on a character that is not the gait -- a look, a flinch -- and can it put it on one part of the body without touching the rest?
cases.expectation: `watcher` is an alien with two animation layers on top of whatever clip the gait machine is playing: an aim layer masked to the five joints that are this rig's head (`head.x`, `Eye_L`, `Eye_R`, `Mouth`, `Antenna`), driven by `LocomotionState::lookTarget`; and an additive layer masked to the upper body playing `Fight_head_hit`, driven by `LocomotionState::reaction`. Walking, with the target at (2, 0, 12), the head group turns **+32.71 deg** and `Eye_L` moves **0.0935** model units while `foot.l`, `foot.r` and `root.x` move **exactly 0.000000** -- the layer wrote 5 joints of 90. Pin the layer's weight to zero and the same second of the same walk has the head **0.000 deg** from where the clip left it; mask the identical layer onto the feet instead and `foot.r` moves **0.1447** while the head moves **0.0000 deg**. On a `music.impact` pulse, `reaction` reads 0.6733, the chest moves 0.0088 and the neck 0.0334, and the feet move 0.000000. Before ADR-300 every one of those numbers was zero, because `lookTarget`, `hasLookTarget` and `reaction` were published every frame and read by nobody.
cases.notes: Asserted by tests/unit/test_character_lab_layers.cpp. The trap this case is built around: `alien-scout.glb` is nearly flat, `head.x` has zero children, and the eyes, mouth and antenna are its siblings -- so the mask "head.x and its descendants" covers 1 joint of 90 and a look-at built on it would turn a head and leave the eyes behind. Three rig families, three names for the head (`head.x`, `Head01`, `Head`), and no joint name is hardcoded anywhere in the engine. Watch the antenna: if it stays pointing the old way while the head turns, the mask has lost a name.

cases.title: Half a metre of landing the engine throws away
cases.question: When a clip moves the character itself -- `Landing` drops the root 0.567 m -- does the body go where the animator put it, or does it play the drop in place?
cases.expectation: In place. ADR-161 concluded there was no root motion in this content to extract, from three clips of one Mixamo file, and the two asset packs that arrived afterwards were never re-checked. Five clips per alien translate their root: `Dying_forward` 0.985 m across and -0.674 m down, `Dying_1_backpack` 0.875 / -0.464, `Dying_1_no_backpack` 0.868 / -0.629, `Crazy` 0.071 / +0.069, and **`Landing` 0.022 / -0.567** -- which Glowmere plays, at the moment a jump resolves. The expectation once P9 lands: with extraction opted in for `Landing`, `watcher`'s simulation position falls by 0.567 m times the node scale over the clip and its feet stay under it; with the opt-in off, the other 163 clips are byte-identical to what they are today.
cases.notes: The inventory is in ADR-260 and the layer stack it needed is in ADR-300; what is missing is the half that writes `MotionAuthority::Simulation`, which `src/scene/pose_layers.*` is deliberately unable to do -- it includes nothing from `entity/`. P9's seam runs the opposite way to the layer stack: a value read back out of the rig into the entity. The trap ADR-260 names: `joints[0]` is an armature wrapper no clip animates, so a probe that takes it as the root reports 168 clips with a root that never moved, for the most boring possible reason.

cases.title: A guard, and no C++ class called Guard
cases.question: Can a character kind that is not an explorer be built out of scene data alone, and can it say what it turned down?
cases.expectation: It can. `guard-post.scene.json` carries three characters and the two that decide are the same C++ class: `sentry` is `holdPost + investigate + idle` and `pilgrim` is `interest + idle`, both reported by `IBehavior::kind()` as **`decide`**, and neither has a line of C++ of its own. At 60 s the guard is **12.10 m** from its post and the explorer **12.66 m** from where it started; the guard scores 3 options on every tick and the explorer scores 7, one per thing it noticed. `holdPost` is one term and not two options -- flat inside `tolerance`, rising at `pull` per metre beyond it -- so 'go back' and 'stay' are the same intention at different distances, and a cooldown is a term in the score rather than a flag (ADR-269). The dwell and the margin are counted and visible: 9 decisions, 0 dwell refusals, 1 margin refusal over 75 s. Play-vs-seek on this scene is **0.036667 m at 30 s** over 3 bodies -- the selector carries a committed choice across frames, which is exactly the thing that could have made that worse, and it is counted in decision ticks rather than accumulated seconds so the boundary lands on the same instant at 60 Hz and at 37 Hz (20 ms apart, one frame of the coarser rate; an accumulated half-second would have drifted 264 ms by four seconds).
cases.notes: Asserted by tests/unit/test_entity_decision.cpp. Two things this fixture cost a wrong answer to find. **A decider must stand off from what it walks to**: a landmark's interest point is at the landmark and a landmark is usually solid, and `NavigatorPath::route` -- the provider the action tier's `move` runs through -- refuses a goal that is not navigable, so the explorer scored six options, committed to one every tick and travelled 0.00 m in 75 s while its queue drained with `unreachable`. `Explore` never met this because it goes through `requestPath`, which carries a goal tolerance. And **a body remembers where it has been, not where it is going**: recording the destination devalues the errand it has just set out on, because the goal model suppresses a visited place to 0.12, and the winner in the overlay was never the highest score.

cases.title: Seven hundred lines moved and the route did not
cases.question: When the only autonomous mind in the engine is refactored, how would anyone know the film had changed?
cases.expectation: By a trace, and not by a walk test. ADR-333 moved `Explore`'s goal model -- five affinities, a distance falloff and a visited-place suppression -- out of the class and into `entity::goalWeight`, where a guard and an explorer weigh a place with one function. `tests/data/explore-position-trace.txt` is **3,600 samples** of the five bodies on this fixture over 60 s at a fixed 60 Hz, every fifth frame, each of x, y, z and yaw as its raw 32 bits, written by the build before the move. After it: **0 lines differ**. Not a tolerance -- bit equality, because the claim is that the arithmetic is the same arithmetic and not that it is close. The control, in the same file and passing before the golden was worth having: one metre on `entity/scout/explore/maxRange` moves **621 of the 3,600 samples**, so the trace is measuring the goal model rather than the fact that characters walk. A second control covers the golden itself -- four of the five bodies must occupy more than one distinct sample, because a golden of five stationary characters would match whatever the extraction did to them.
cases.notes: Asserted by tests/unit/test_decision_extraction.cpp. The weighted roll deliberately did **not** move: it draws from `Entity::rng_`, which is a stream, and D2 exists because one extra draw re-casts every later choice. Replacing it with the selector's argmax would change every route in Glowmere, so the extraction is of the model and not of the choice -- see ADR-333 section 4 for what unifying them would cost. Regenerating the golden is deliberately awkward (`AVGEN_WRITE_EXPLORE_GOLDEN=1`) and is a statement that a route was meant to change.
